title: Find Closest Node to Given Two Nodes
summary: Given a directed graph with nodes numbered from 0 to n-1, where each node has at most one outgoing edge, and two specific nodes node1 and node2, find the node that can be reached from both node1 and node2.
statement: Given a directed graph with nodes numbered from 0 to n-1, where each node has at most one outgoing edge, and two specific nodes node1 and node2, find the node that can be reached from both node1 and node2. The goal is to minimize the maximum distance from either node1 or node2 to the reached node. If there are multiple such nodes, return the one with the smallest index. If no such node exists, return -1. The graph is represented by an array of size n, where edges[i] indicates the destination of the outgoing edge from node i, or -1 if no such edge exists.
constraints: Node i has one directed edge to edges[i], or no outgoing edge when edges[i] is -1.
Among nodes reachable from both starts, minimize the larger of the two path distances.
Break equal maximum distances by returning the smaller node index; return -1 if no common node exists.
hints: Walk forward from each start and record the first distance to every visited node.
Stop a walk at -1 or at a previously visited node, which also handles cycles.
Scan node indexes in ascending order and keep a common node only when its maximum distance strictly improves.
The two walks give exact reachable distances; the scan evaluates the objective for every common node and its strict update preserves the smallest-index tie break.

tests.explanation: Both starts reach node 2 in one step, so its maximum distance is one and it is optimal.
Node 2 is reachable from both starts; its distances are two and zero, so the answer is 2.
